title: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models
one_line_claim: Hybrid quantization-eviction KV cache compression that preserves high-precision tokens from critical reasoning steps while discarding less important ones, achieving up to 5.8x throughput improvement.
method_summary: ThinKV applies hybrid quantization and eviction to KV caches by analyzing attention sparsity to identify thought types within chain-of-thought reasoning. Tokens from critical reasoning steps are preserved at high precision while tokens from less critical thoughts are progressively evicted. A custom kernel extends PagedAttention to enable efficient memory reuse without compaction overhead.

key_findings.finding: ThinKV achieves near-lossless accuracy with less than 5% of the original KV cache size.
key_findings.quote: near-lossless accuracy with less than 5% of the original KV cache

key_findings.finding: Delivers up to 5.8x higher inference throughput compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
key_findings.quote: up to 5.8x higher inference throughput over state-of-the-art baselines

key_findings.finding: Attention sparsity patterns reveal distinct thought types with varying importance within chain-of-thought reasoning.
key_findings.quote: attention sparsity reveals distinct thought types with varying importance within the CoT

relation_to_herald.shared: Both target KV-cache compression in LLM inference and identify token-level importance signals (attention patterns vs. logit features) to guide compression or hazard decisions.
differs_on: ThinKV uses attention sparsity as the compression signal; HERALD uses per-token logit distributions and entropy as failure predictors.
ThinKV applies selective quantization and eviction; HERALD predicts catastrophic failures to enable intervention rather than applying static compression.
ThinKV's compression decisions are deterministic from attention patterns; HERALD's prediction is probabilistic via XGBoost on time-series logit features.
